newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER-LEVERKUSEN BACK ON TRACK WITH FIRST WIN.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-LEVERKUSEN BACK ON TRACK WITH FIRST WIN.

text.p: Bayer Leverkusen, runners-up in the German championship last season, made good for Friday's defeat at Schalke with a hard-fought victory against Bochum in their second game of the new season on Tuesday.

Leverkusen came out 3-2 winners with an 85th-minute goal by Carsten Ramelow, allowing them to escape a repeat of last season's December clash, when Bochum managed a 2-2 draw that cost Leverkusen valuable title points.

After dominating the first half, Bochum had gone one goal up with a strike from Sergej Juran in the 37th minute, but Leverkusen pulled into the lead with second-half headers from Ulf Kirsten and Erik Meijer.
Bochum managed to equalise with a goal by Mirko Dickhaut but Ramelow finally stole the honours for Leverkusen.

Karlsruhe's 2-2 draw at 1860 Munich was enough to see them creep into an early lead at the top of the table, but with eight clubs still to play their second matches on Wednesday, including champions Bayern Munich, that lead looks shaky.
